title: Leaf count after deleting a subprotocol branch
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic communication protocol and let $s$ be a rooted subtree of $p$, witnessed by a subprotocol path from the root of $p$ down to the root of $s$. Write $\ell(r)$ for the number of leaves (output nodes) of a protocol $r$. If deleting this branch splices out a proper subtree — that is, if the deletion produces a protocol $q$ rather than the empty result of the root case — then \[ \ell(q) = \ell(p) - \ell(s), \] where the subtraction is truncated subtraction on $\bbn$.
hypotheses_covered: s is a rooted subtree of p, given by a subprotocol path from s to p
the deletion of this path yields some protocol q (the non-root case)
